body:
## Summary Compiling a Triton kernel that calls `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` inside a `for`-loop whose body also contains a `tl.dot` consuming the descriptor load fails at JIT compile time on the NVIDIA backend with: ``` error: 'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op. LLVM ERROR: Fatal pipeliner error error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline note: Pipeline failed while executing [`TritonGPUPipeline` on 'builtin.module' operation] ``` Reproduces on every NVIDIA GPU we tested: B200 (sm_100, Blackwell) and H200 NVL (sm_90, Hopper). ## Environment | Component | Version | |-------------------|-------------------------------------------------| | Triton | `3.6.0` (also reproduces on `3.7.0+git886365ca` nightly from `triton-lang/triton` Actions run 25312905392) | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu130` | | CUDA (runtime) | `13.0` | | NVIDIA driver | `580.126.09` (B200 host) and `580.105.08` (H200 host) — both on the 580 driver line; `cuDriverGetVersion` returns `13000` inside the container in both cases | | GPUs tested | NVIDIA B200 (sm_100, Blackwell), NVIDIA H200 NVL (sm_90, Hopper) | | Docker base image | `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (digest `sha256:04563c302537a91aa49ebdfbceda96111c5712275999b7e8804fa598f0b5641d`) | | Python | 3.12 | ## Reproducer Self-contained script (no vLLM / flash-attention dependency; pure Triton + torch), full source below. Run command: ```bash docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0"' \ -v "$(pwd)/minimal_tma_pipeliner_repro.py:/tmp/repro.py:ro" \ --entrypoint python3 vllm/vllm-openai:latest /tmp/repro.py ``` Expected output: ``` [info] compiling kernel... /tmp/repro.py:62:12: error: 'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op. LLVM ERROR: Fatal pipeliner error [fail] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ```
minimal_tma_pipeliner_repro.py (115 lines) ```python """Minimal reproducer: tl.make_tensor_descriptor + tl.dot inside a pipelined for-loop fails to compile on the Triton NVIDIA backend. Environment tested: * Triton 3.6.0 (also 3.7.0+git886365ca nightly) * torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA driver 580.126.09 * B200 sm_100, H200 NVL sm_90 * Python 3.12, docker: vllm/vllm-openai:latest Error: error: 'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op. LLVM ERROR: Fatal pipeliner error Run (no vLLM needed, just torch + triton in the container): docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0"' \\ -v "$(pwd)/minimal_tma_pipeliner_repro.py:/tmp/repro.py:ro" \\ --entrypoint python3 vllm/vllm-openai:latest /tmp/repro.py """ from __future__ import annotations import torch import triton import triton.language as tl def _alloc_fn(size: int, align: int, _stream) -> torch.Tensor: return torch.empty(size, dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda") try: triton.set_allocator(_alloc_fn) except AttributeError: pass @triton.jit def kernel_td_matmul( out_ptr, q_ptr, k_cache_ptr, stride_0: tl.int64, stride_1: tl.int64, stride_2: tl.constexpr, num_tiles: tl.int64, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, TILE_SIZE: tl.constexpr, HEAD_SIZE: tl.constexpr, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED: tl.constexpr, ): q_vec = tl.load(q_ptr + tl.arange(0, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED)).reshape( 1, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED ) acc = tl.zeros((1, TILE_SIZE), dtype=tl.float32) for j in range(num_tiles): desc = tl.make_tensor_descriptor( base=k_cache_ptr + j * stride_0, shape=(BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE), strides=(stride_1, stride_2), block_shape=(TILE_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED), ) K_tile = desc.load([0, 0]) K_T = tl.trans(K_tile) acc += tl.dot(q_vec, K_T).to(tl.float32) tl.store(out_ptr + tl.arange(0, TILE_SIZE), acc.reshape(TILE_SIZE)) def main() -> int: if not torch.cuda.is_available(): raise SystemExit("no CUDA device available") BLOCK_SIZE = 16 TILE_SIZE = 16 HEAD_SIZE = 64 HEAD_SIZE_PADDED = 64 num_blocks = 32 num_tiles = 8 torch.manual_seed(0) q = torch.randn(HEAD_SIZE_PADDED, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) k = torch.randn( num_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16 ) out = torch.zeros(TILE_SIZE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) print("[info] compiling kernel...") try: kernel_td_matmul[(1,)]( out_ptr=out, q_ptr=q, k_cache_ptr=k, stride_0=k.stride(0), stride_1=k.stride(1), stride_2=k.stride(2), num_tiles=num_tiles, BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE, TILE_SIZE=TILE_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE=HEAD_SIZE, HEAD_SIZE_PADDED=HEAD_SIZE_PADDED, ) torch.cuda.synchronize() except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 first = str(exc).splitlines()[0] if str(exc) else "(no msg)" print(f"[fail] {type(exc).__name__}: {first}") return 1 print(f"[pass] kernel compiled and ran, out[:4]={out[:4].cpu().tolist()}") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main()) ```
## Empirical reduction The offending pattern was identified by step-down from a larger kernel. Results on B200 / driver 580.x / Triton 3.6.0: | # | Kernel shape | Result | |---|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------| | 1 | single `tl.make_tensor_descriptor`, no loop | PASS | | 2 | single descriptor inside `for`-loop, reduction only (no `tl.dot`) | PASS | | 3 | two descriptors inside `for`-loop, reduction only (no `tl.dot`) | PASS | | 4 | single descriptor inside `for`-loop under `if USE_TD:` (no `tl.dot`) | PASS | | 5 | single descriptor + `tl.dot` consuming the load (attached reproducer) | FAIL | | 6 | two descriptors + matmul + flash-attention softmax prelude | FAIL | Required triggers, both necessary: - `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` inside a `for`-loop, **and** - a `tl.dot` in the same loop body that consumes the descriptor load. Not required: second descriptor, constexpr gate, softmax, running-max state, warp specialization. ## Our reading of the root cause `TritonGPUPipeline` only runs on a `for`-loop when the body has a `tl.dot` (that's the purpose of pipelining — overlap TMA loads with the matmul). Inside that pipelined loop the `triton-nvidia-tma-lowering` pass turns `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` into a host-side `ttng.tensormap_create` op. Pipelining then needs to place `tensormap_create` under the predicate it generates for the staged iteration schedule, and the NVIDIA backend explicitly bails. Workarounds that do compile: - remove `tl.dot` from the loop (no pipelining runs), - hoist the descriptor out of the loop (no predicate needed), - switch to pointer-arithmetic / `tl.load` with masks (no TD at all). ## Pipeline reported in the diagnostic dump Excerpt from the `mlir_reproducer` block Triton printed to stderr (B200 run; the H200 run emits the same pass chain with `target=cuda:90` instead of `cuda:100`, and fails at the same `TritonGPUPipeline` pass): ``` pipeline: "builtin.module( convert-triton-to-tritongpu{... target=cuda:100 ...}, tritongpu-coalesce, ... triton-nvidia-optimize-descriptor-encoding, tritongpu-fuse-nested-loops, ... triton-nvidia-tma-lowering, ... tritongpu-pipeline{num-stages=3}, ... )" ``` ## Python-side traceback ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/repro.py", line 106, in main kernel_td_matmul[(1,)](...) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 720, in run kernel = self._do_compile( File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 849, in _do_compile kernel = self.compile(src, target=target, options=options.__dict__) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 324, in compile next_module = compile_ir(module, metadata) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py", line 541, in stages["ttgir"] = lambda src, metadata: self.make_ttgir( src, metadata, options, capability ) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/nvidia/compiler.py", line 316, in make_ttgir pm.run(mod, 'make_ttgir') RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Happy to share the full MLIR reproducer (`mlir_reproducer` block Triton emits to stderr) and the untruncated stderr if it helps. ## Related open issue Closest existing match I could find: [#7786](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/issues/7786) ("triton 3.4.0 tma load error in the loop `make_tensor_descriptor`") — same area, different exact error signature, open since 2025-08 with no fix. Possibly the same root cause, filing separately because the `'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate` signature did not show up in any open or closed issue I searched. ## Context Distilled from [vllm-project/vllm#40327](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40327) (opt-in tensor-descriptor path in Triton unified attention, primarily shipped for Intel XPU). On the NVIDIA side of that PR the TD path is gated behind an explicit `VLLM_TRITON_ATTN_USE_TD=1` opt-in precisely because of this compile failure — default NVIDIA users are not affected, but anyone opting in (or anyone else wiring `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` + `tl.dot` into the same pipelined loop) will hit this. ## Asks - Is the error expected, i.e. is `ttng.tensormap_create` known to be unpredicable by the current `TritonGPUPipeline`? If so, what is the recommended pattern for per-tile TMA descriptors inside a pipelined matmul loop — hoist them into a precomputed table of descriptors, or fall back to `tl.load` with masks? - If it is a bug in the pass ordering / predicate implementation, happy to help with any extra info (full IR dump, a smaller repro, or testing candidate fixes on our B200 / H200).
title: Triton NVIDIA backend: 'ttng.tensormap_create' op pipeliner doesn't know how to predicate this op (CUDA 13.0, sm_90 + sm_100)
